title: Extracting the pairing gap from van Hove singularities in rf spectra of the Fermi Hubbard model
authors: Chuping Li, Kaichao Zhang, Junru Wu, Yuxuan Wu, Dingli Yuan, Pengyi Chen, Lin Sun, Qijin Chen
abstract: We show that van Hove singularities in rf spectra of the 3D attractive Fermi Hubbard model provide a robust route to extracting the pairing gap. Four types of singularities are classified, and their spectral positions are shown to depend solely on the pairing gap $Δ$ and chemical potential $μ$ through simple algebraic relations. Measuring two well-resolved singularities therefore determines both parameters without requiring full spectral fitting. Numerical simulations incorporating phenomenological lifetime and scattering broadenings confirm that these features remain visible in both momentum-integrated and $k_z$-integrated spectra, and become more pronounced at stronger coupling where conventional back-bending methods lose sensitivity. At half filling, particle-hole symmetry fixes $μ$, reducing the extraction to a single singularity measurement. These results establish vHS analysis as a practical spectroscopic diagnostic for pairing in quantum-simulated 3D Fermi Hubbard systems.
summary: The authors propose using van Hove singularities (vHSs) observed in the rf spectra of the 3D attractive Fermi Hubbard model as a highly robust method to determine the pairing gap ($\Delta$) and chemical potential ($\mu$). By showing that vHS positions depend only on these two parameters, measuring just two distinct features allows for parameter extraction without needing full spectral fitting. This establishes vHS analysis as a practical diagnostic tool for quantum simulation experiments.
main_problem: The primary goal is to establish a robust spectroscopic method for extracting the pairing gap ($\Delta$) from radio-frequency (rf) spectra of the Fermi Hubbard model.
main_result: Van Hove singularities (vHSs) in the rf spectra depend only on $\Delta$ and chemical potential $\mu$, allowing both parameters to be determined by measuring just two well-resolved vHS positions.
method:
The analysis uses linear response theory applied to the low-order rf current, identifying characteristic detunings ($
u_i$) at vHS momenta derived from the Green's function formalism.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the 3D attractive Fermi Hubbard model, relevant for ultracold Fermi gases in optical lattices. The theory extends beyond mean-field BCS by using pair-fluctuation theory within the T-matrix approximation.
key_observables:
Van Hove singularities (vHSs) in the rf spectral function $A(\mathbf{k}, \omega)$, characterized by specific detuning values ($
u_i$).
important_parameters: Pairing gap ($\Delta$), chemical potential ($\mu$), interaction strength ($|U|$), and lattice hopping ($t$). Special attention is paid to the half-filling case where $\mu$ is fixed.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that vHS features remain visible even when incorporating phenomenological lifetime and scattering broadenings, allowing for algebraic extraction of parameters from kinematic relations.
figures_summary:
Figures illustrate representative spectral functions showing particle/hole branches (Fig 1), the momentum-integrated rf current with labeled vHS features (Fig 2), and how these detunings ($
u_i$) vary systematically with interaction strength and filling (Fig 8).
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by deriving the dependence of vHS positions on $\Delta$ and $\mu$, demonstrating that two such measurements suffice for parameter extraction. It then analyzes the robustness of this method across different momentum resolutions and coupling strengths.
why_interesting: This provides a concrete, measurable spectroscopic diagnostic tool for characterizing superfluidity in quantum simulators, offering an alternative to complex full spectral fitting techniques.
